Application Materials.content:
- An updated Resume
- Your official academic transcripts of all educational institutions attended.
- Certified True Copies of CFA / ACCA certificates (if any)
- **2 Personal Statements (approximately 500-600 words each)** on the following topics:
1. Explain your career and personal aspirations, and your motivation for pursuing the MSc in Wealth Management (MWM) programme.
2. Discuss one of the following topics:
1. Describe your greatest weakness and how you have tried to overcome it.
2. Describe your outstanding talents, skills and inherent abilities that are not reflected in your academic qualifications and records.
- **2 Referee Reports** - Submit 2 complete sets of referee details during the online process of applying for the SMU MWM. The application portal will automatically send an email to your referees and collect your recommendation forms on your behalf once you have submitted the application.
- Copy of NRIC/FIN/Passport (in PDF or JPEG format).
- Any other supporting documents.
- Verification of original documents is required upon matriculation into the programme. Failing to do so may result in applicants having to withdraw from the programme.
- Leadership scholarship essay: “Please explain in 500 words why you consider yourself a leader"
- Impact on Asia scholarship essay: “Please explain in 500 words the professional development, entrepreneurial or personal projects of an Asian focus, that have contributed positively to Asian regions or companies or have increased awareness of Asia in other locations."
- Women in Business scholarship essay: “Please explain in 500 words why you should be awarded with the Women in Business Scholarship”.
- Community Impact scholarship essay: “Please share an example of how you have impacted your greater community and what you think is the best way to serve society."

Interview Requirements.content:
- Shortlisted candidates will be invited for an **online interview within two weeks of the application**.
- All shortlisted candidates need to go through **panel interview by the Admissions Committee**.

Application Deadlines.content:
- Application period: **Now to End-May 2026**.
- Intake/admissions cycle: **August 2026** — Now to **End-May 2026**. Early applications are encouraged in view of rolling admissions.
- [Apply Now](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/MWM/Apply_now)

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Bachelor's Degree** / **good undergraduate degree (in any field)** is required for the MSc in Wealth Management (MWM).
- Applicants require **at least 2 years of working experience in any industry (post-bachelor degree)**. A waiver is considered for applicants who have passed **CFA Level 1**.
- FAQ admission criteria: applicants require **a good university degree, and two or more years of working experience in any industry**. For applicants with less than two years of working experience, preference will be given to those who attain a pass in the **Chartered Financial Analysts (CFA) Level 1 examination**.
- Candidates should be “keen to stay at the frontier of global investing and have a passion for a career in wealth management.”
- Admissions selection takes into consideration “your work experience, past performance, first degree, admissions test score, and your drive and motivation.”
- **SMU graduates with cumulative GPAs of 3.0/4.0 or better**, and graduates from local Autonomous Universities **(NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, SIT) with cumulative GPAs of 3.5/5.0 or better** will not require a GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test score for admissions. An undergraduate GPA is valid for **5 years after graduation**. Meeting the above GPA academic criteria does not guarantee admission.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
- **GMAT / GRE / SMU Admissions Test** is listed as a pre-requisite for the Master of Science in Wealth Management (MWM).
- Applicants must submit **a good GMAT / GRE / SMU Admissions Test (SMUAT) score**; the [SMUAT Factsheet](https://postgraduate.smu.edu.sg/acton/attachment/11522/f-4aba8d35-81c0-41d8-860f-8aa1c29d5d03/1/-/-/-/-/SMU%20Admissions%20Test%20Fact%20Sheet.pdf) is linked on the application page.
- **SMU graduates with cumulative GPAs of 3.0/4.0 or better**, and graduates from local Autonomous Universities (NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, SIT) with **cumulative GPAs of 3.5/5.0 or better** will not require a GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test score for admissions. An undergraduate GPA is valid for **5 years after graduation**. Meeting the GPA academic criteria does not guarantee admission; candidates may still be advised to submit GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test scores to further strengthen their application.
- FAQ: “An admissions test (GMAT/GRE/ SMU Admissions Test) is a compulsory requirement for admission to this programme.”
- FAQ: “We have not set a minimum GMAT/GRE score. We adopt a holistic approach to applications for admission to this programme.”
- Applicants may apply before taking GMAT/GRE if the rest of the application is completed; they should send the unofficial score as soon as received and arrange for the official score report to be sent to SMU. **SMU GMAT institution code is F8D-7V-34 and the GRE institution code is 5757.**
- Applicants are allowed to take the **SMU Admissions Test** as an alternative to the GMAT or GRE.
- **GMAT/GRE score is valid for 5 years after the test date.**

English Proficiency Requirements.content: TOEFL / IELTS (if the medium of instruction of your undergraduate studies was not English)

Program Overview.content:
- Complete within 12 months over five study blocks
- Specialised curriculum in global wealth management with an Asian focus
- First MSc in Wealth Management programme in Asia
- Master’s degree awarded by SMU; certificates awarded by eminient universities in Switzerland and USA.
- Experienced faculty drawn from senior academics with industry experience and successful wealth professionals with academic exposure
- Closely connected with the wealth management industry for engagements in placements, corporate boards, scholarships and guest lecturing
- Modular structure allows participants to meet their professional and personal obligations while pursuing an academic degree
- Pedagogy includes case studies, team activities, pre-course assignments, computer-aided learning, simulations, industry talks, site visits and field trips to complement classroom learning
- A preparatory module designed to prepare students before the first study block
- Completion of an individual project by participants on a research topic of interest
- Opportunities to intern in various financial institutes during the one-year period
- Recognised by the CFA Institute and CAIA as a collaborative partner

Curriculum.content:
- The Master of Science in Wealth Management (MWM) has a **12-month duration (Modular)** and is completed within 12 months.
- The programme comprises five study blocks where classes will be conducted on **Wednesday evenings, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays**.
- Students are required to attend an overseas segment at **University of St. Gallen (HSG)** and **Cambridge Judge Business School** for two consecutive weeks during the fourth study block.
- The graduation requirement is **15 Credit Units (CUs)** and a minimum CGPA of **2.5**. The core curriculum consists of **15 CUs**.
- Students undergo a preparatory module before the first study block, and the programme culminates in the completion of an **individual project on a research topic of your choosing**.
- Classroom learning is complemented by case studies, team activities, pre-course assignments, computer-aided learning, simulations, industry talks, site visits and field trips. The programme’s modular structure allows students to meet professional and personal obligations while pursuing an academic degree.
- Internship is optional and can be done any time during the period of study. Students have the opportunity upon application to intern in various financial institutes during a one-year period.
**Preparatory Modules**
- Jul Prep & Induction: Online Matriculation; Boot Camp; Orientation and Team Building.
**Core Modules**
- Aug Study Block I: Financial Statement Analysis; Macroeconomics and Global Financial Markets; Quant Methods for Investment Analysis; Corporate Finance.
- Oct Study Block II: Analysis of Equities and ETF; Analysis of Fixed Income; Analysis & Applications of Derivatives.
- Jan Study Block III: Portfolio Management; Wealth Planning; Advanced Topics in Wealth Management; Financial Advisers Law & Compliance.
- Mar-Apr Study Block IV: Advanced Wealth Planning; Private Equity & Venture Capital; Fintech in Wealth Management; Alternative Investing; European Family Offices.
- May-Jun Study Block V: Structured Products; Client Relationship Management; Client Book Reading; Investment Management in Family Office; Seminar in Wealth Management.
If you do not have a background in wealth management, you will be encouraged to take up internships. A number of corporations are offering to host potential candidates as interns for different durations, ranging from three months to the entire length of the 12-month programme. Internships may incorporate exposure to different aspects of wealth management, briefings and tours of departments, brief assignments during rotations through departments, and attachment to a senior officer as mentor.

Living expenses will vary depending on your lifestyle and accommodation. However, the average international student would be able to stay within a monthly budget of S$2000 - with change to spare. Estimated breakdown of basic living expenses:

| --- | --- |
| **Accommodation** | **S$250 - S$800** |
| **Utilities** | **S$40 - S$100** |
| **Transportation** | **S$200** |
| **Telecommunications** | **S$50** |
| **Books & Stationery** | **S$200 per term** |
| **Personal Expenses (mobile phone, meals, etc)** | **S$100 - S$300** |
| **Food** | **S$300 - S$450** |

Financial Aid.content:
Scholarships are available based on merit for selected participants.
Academic Excellence | Global Awareness | Leadership* | Impact on Asia* | Women in Business* | Community Impact* | Keeve Tan Wealth Management Scholarship*
_* Denotes scholarships that students can apply for upon admissions into the programme._ These scholarships entail award amounts up to **S$18,000**, with no bonds attached.
- Keeve Tan Wealth Management Scholarship: supports talented Southeast Asian students with demonstrated academic excellence, and relevant work experience in asset or wealth management. Benefits: **$20,000**, tenable for one academic year.
- MWM Talent Development Scholarship: awarded to eligible individuals of any nationality who are currently working in a private bank or related financial institution, with at least five years of experience in financial or wealth management, and who are either company-sponsored or SMU alumni. MWMTD Scholarship quantum: **S$18,000 (inclusive of GST)**. Candidates are automatically submitted for consideration for MWMTD scholarship upon meeting the scholarship and application criteria. Scholarship is awarded on a highly selective and competitive basis. Terms include: bond free; all application documents must be submitted by the application deadline; successful candidates must matriculate and start the MWM in the same applied intake; no deferment, withdrawal, leave of absence during the one-year study is allowed.
- IBF-STS funding will range from **S$17,000 to S$19,000** for Singapore Citizens and Singapore PRs who have successfully completed the SMU MWM programme. Eligible students will receive the funding as a reduction to their second billing of tuition fees.
- Academic Excellence Award: offered to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and admissions test score. Awardees must have achieved an excellent admissions test score (equivalent to GMAT score of **700 and above**) and have demonstrated outstanding academic achievement.
- Global Awareness Award: given to individuals who will contribute to classroom diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of their cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
- Leadership Award: recognises individuals with strong leadership capabilities who have exhibited outstanding leadership capabilities and potential during their studies, community or organisation. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership potential in personal and professional instances.
- Impact on Asia Award: for students who can demonstrate achievements in their professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia.
- Women in Business Award: recognises exceptional women who have demonstrated outstanding leadership capabilities or potential in their professional or personal endeavours. Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer.
- Community Impact Award: recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and through their actions have impacted members of the community/society in a positive manner.
- SkillsFuture: SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme provides Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above the opportunity to receive the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top up of **$4,000** to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after **1 May 2024**.
- CIMB ASEAN Scholarship: Learn more and apply for the CIMB ASEAN Scholarship [here.](https://www.cimb.com/en/careers/students/cimb-asean-scholarship.html)
- SMU Alumni: graduates from SMU undergraduate or postgraduate programmes are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$8,000** when applying to the MWM programme.
- Singapore Local Autonomous University: graduates from NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, or SIT are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$4,000** when applying to the MWM programme. Eligible candidates may receive exemptions for up to four credit units, with a discount of **$3,000** awarded for each credit unit exempted.
- SG/PR: Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$5,000**.
- ASEAN Citizens: ASEAN citizens are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$3,000**.
- Corporate Partner: eligible company-sponsored candidates are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$6,000**. If 2 or more company-sponsored candidates from the same organisation are enrolling in the same intake, each will enjoy a **S$12,000** discount. If a company which has previously sponsored an employee is sponsoring another employee into the programme at a subsequent intake, that employee will enjoy a **S$9,000** discount off the total tuition fee.
The discounts are applicable to students joining the programme from the January 2025 intake onwards. Each student is only eligible for one discount; should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount will be applicable. The tuition fee discount is deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST).

Multiple Applications.content: If you have applied for more than one programme, you are only required to take the test once. Please contact your first-choice’s programme office to register for the test and update the other programme office upon the completion of your test via email to ensure timely processing of all your SMU applications.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: MWM Talent Development Scholarship Terms & Conditions: successful candidates must matriculate and start the MWM in the same applied intake. **No deferment** during the one-year study is allowed.
